ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: When the duration of sunlight gradually lengthens in spring, most birds enter the breeding season. The diagram regulating bird reproductive activities is as shown in the figure. Question: In the figure, A, B, and C respectively represent substances secreted by the hypothalamus, pituitary gland, and gonads, so what are they respectively?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the regulation process starts from “light,” and sequentially passes through “receptor” and “afferent nerve” to reach the “hypothalamus”; after the hypothalamus, the substance labeled A acts on the “pituitary gland”; after the pituitary gland, the substance labeled B acts on the “gonads”; the gonads then secrete the substance labeled C. In the figure, feedback regulation arrows returning from later links to higher-level centers can also be seen. Then reason: The question stem states that A, B, and C respectively represent substances secreted by the hypothalamus, pituitary gland, and gonads. Bird reproductive activities are regulated by the hypothalamus-pituitary-gonad axis: the hypothalamus secretes gonadotropin-releasing hormone, promoting pituitary gland activity; the pituitary gland secretes gonadotropin, promoting gonad activity; the gonads secrete sex hormones, regulating reproductive activities. Therefore, A is gonadotropin-releasing hormone, B is gonadotropin, and C is sex hormone.
